reasons.why: Windows paths in configuration (drive letters, UNC shares) are overridden with environment variables to folders under /data, which the manifests mount as volumes; the application code is not changed.
The app logs to files under its own folder; the folder is made writable so start-up does not fail on the read-only root file system (console logging is preferred).

A dependency built for netstandard1.x pins System.* 4.0.x packages (SSH.NET 2016.x directly; Microsoft.Azure.Amqp 2.5.6 through System.Net.WebSockets.Client 4.0.2, pulled in by Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus 7.5.0 and MassTransit.Azure.ServiceBus.Core 7.3). Restoring for the linux-x64 runtime identifier adds runtime.unix.* packages that need 4.3.0, which NuGet reports as a package downgrade (NU1605, an error in SDK builds). A portable publish (no -r) restores the same graph as the Windows build and runs on the Linux runtime image. Upgrading the package (SSH.NET 2020.0.0+, a current Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus) removes the conflict.
